title: Senior Applied AI Solutions Engineer
description:
About Nebius :

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

AI is moving faster than any single product team can track. Nebius is expanding across serverless, databases, MLflow, MLOps, Physical AI, and HCLS — and customers arriving with complex, real-world ML workloads need more than documentation. This role exists to close that gap: someone who can prototype what's possible, accelerate customers through their first 90 days, and feed hard-won field insight back into the product roadmap.
This role sits at the intersection of deep ML engineering and product impact. You'll spend roughly half your time in the field — helping new customers move from POC to production, running technical onboarding, and working hands-on through their ML stack. The other half you'll spend building — prototyping applied AI use cases that show what's possible on the platform, going deep on emerging techniques before they're mainstream, and turning that expertise into concrete product direction.
This is not a presales role. You get your hands dirty every day.

What success looks like in 12 months

The product and sales teams have a library of working, polished demos they reach for on calls

Enterprise customers you've touched have meaningfully faster time-to-value than those you haven't

At least 2–3 product changes were shipped because of feedback you originated

The team understands where applied AI is heading 6–12 months from now, partly because you told them

Your responsibilities will include:

Build prototypes and demos across the product portfolio — serverless inference, databases, MLflow, MLOps, and vertical use cases in Physical AI and HCLS — that become assets for sales, product, and engineering teams

Support new customers hands-on through POC design, technical onboarding, and validation; act as the bridge between their ML team and the platform during the critical first months

Go deep on emerging applied AI — new training techniques, inference optimizations, agentic architectures, new frameworks — and turn findings into working prototypes, writeups, and product recommendations

Feed the product roadmap with specific, grounded feedback; be the voice of "here's what broke in three customer POCs last month and here's what needs to change"

Develop reusable technical assets — notebooks, reference architectures, benchmark results — that reduce onboarding friction at scale

We expect you to have:

You've fine-tuned large models, debugged distributed training jobs, built production RAG or agentic pipelines, and optimized inference on GPU infrastructure — not just read about it

You're fluent in the modern ML stack: PyTorch, HuggingFace, CUDA fundamentals, Kubernetes for ML, MLflow or equivalent, vector databases

You've worked with enterprise ML teams — whether as a solutions engineer, customer engineer, or an ML engineer who collaborated closely with customers

You read papers and implement them — not for credit, but because it's how you stay sharp

You communicate with calibration: you can explain activation checkpointing tradeoffs to an ML engineer in the morning and the cost implication to a CTO in the afternoon

It will be an added bonus if you have:

Experience in any of our vertical domains: Physical AI / robotics / simulation, HCLS (drug discovery, medical imaging, clinical NLP), or enterprise AI application development

Familiarity with MLOps at scale (Kubeflow, Metaflow, Argo, Ray)

Prior work at a cloud provider or AI infrastructure company

You've shared technical work publicly — notebooks, talks, blog posts that people actually use

Who thrives here

You'll thrive here if you're energized by variety — one day deep in a customer's MLOps stack, the next building a demo from scratch. You want your technical depth to influence product decisions, not just close deals.

Your time is a balance between working on features, bugs and resolving technical debt.

Along the way, make what you build safe to change. Restructure and test the paths you build on while you build on them. Extend test coverage where it's lacking. We move fast and keep quality up by automating what a human doesn't need to do, including the checks that catch what an agent got wrong.

Design and build frontend features starting from rough product ideas

Deliver features with Claude Code, from the prompt through to the pull request, and review the output as closely as a colleague's

Ship in short cycles with your product team

Pair, review, and teach what you know

Frontend in Angular, backend in PHP, a web app and a mobile app in React Native. Tests in Jest and Playwright. title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer (Web + Infrastructure)
description:
Searoutes makes the emissions data that shippers use to run and reduce their
logistics. It is an operational problem before it is an environmental one, and
in our hands it is mostly an engineering one.

We are hiring a senior engineer who works across our web frontend and our
infrastructure — the same two codebases, in the same week. Someone who ships a
product screen on Monday, changes an identity-provider flow on Wednesday, and
considers those the same job.

We are looking for a broad profile rather than a specialist. The next year is
mostly platform work with a user-facing edge — user management, API gateway
management, payments, SEO, and a great deal of compliance, GDPR and ISO 27001.

If you are passionate about the environment, proactive and pragmatic in getting
things done, and love to work in a complex but fascinating industry where you
learn every day — then this is the place for you.

The work in front of us

Some of the items on our tech roadmap for the coming year. Bets are picked a
cycle at a time and shared out, so you would take the ones that suit you and
grow into the rest.

Product and marketing UI in React — multi-brand, WCAG AA, strong on
technical SEO, fast enough to hold a performance budget.
User management and identity — Keycloak realms, organisation hierarchies,
partner brokering, and the entitlement model in the app.
API gateway work in APISIX — routes, plugins and auth policy as code.
Payments and billing.
ISO 27001 and GDPR — access control, change management, audit logging,
observability and alerting, consent and retention.
The infrastructure underneath — Pulumi in TypeScript, Docker Swarm on
Hetzner, Cloudflare at the edge, Tailscale for all engineer and CI access.
Third-party integrations — usually the seam between two systems that were
never designed to meet.

Nobody arrives fluent in all of that, and we are not expecting it. We want
someone strong across a good part of it, comfortable being new to the rest, and
used to working things out — with a team and with agents, rather than alone.

Also in daily use: Postgres and PostGIS, Valkey, ClickHouse; Vite, Tailwind and
Radix; Jest and Playwright; GitHub Actions; HAProxy. Most of what we write is
TypeScript, strict — though our core API is Java and Spring, and the identity
layer has Java in it too, so how far you go into that side is up to you.

How we work

LLM-native, in the codebases you would work in. They are built around
agent-assisted development rather than merely tolerant of it — the conventions,
the tooling and the review gates all assume it. Agents do most of the
implementation and much of the review; humans design, verify and approve. What
we are really hiring for is judgement over output you did not write by hand :
knowing what to specify, what to check, and what to throw away. The bar did not
move when the tooling did.

Shape Up, and you own what you take. Roughly three weeks of building, then a
week of cooldown, with bets chosen at a betting table. We are small enough that
an area becomes yours quickly — you make the calls inside it and you answer for
how it turns out. We hand out problems, not the steps that solve them.

Remote first, with most of the team in Europe and everyone together in person at
least twice a year. Significant technical decisions get written down, and a
green build is never on its own enough to merge.
Requirements
You'll thrive here if you have…

Senior full-stack experience — you have owned features from the browser to
the machine they run on.
A track record of taking something and running with it — a domain, a
migration, a subsystem you took on, decided and stayed accountable for.
Taste. You can tell a good design from a merely plausible one, and you
will reject work that functions but is not right — your own, and an agent's.
React beyond the client — server rendering, static generation, data
loading and hydration; you know what runs where and why it matters.
TypeScript at strict — typed boundaries, and an instinct for when types
are carrying real weight.
Infrastructure as code — Pulumi ideally; Terraform if you are ready to
pick up Pulumi.
Containers and Linux in production — not writing a Dockerfile, but
debugging a service on a machine you have to SSH into.
Postgres beyond queries — backup and restore, migrations, what a schema
change does under load.
Wholehearted LLM-assisted development — you use coding agents daily, have
opinions about steering them, and review their output as critically as a
colleague's.
Integration instincts — third-party APIs, webhooks, OAuth/OIDC, and
patience for other people's undocumented edge cases.
A working day that overlaps ours : based within CET ±3.
Fluent in English, our working language.

Nice to have

Identity and API gateways in depth — Keycloak, OIDC, SAML brokering, APISIX.
Compliance from the inside — an ISO 27001 certification lived through, or GDPR
beyond a cookie banner.
Payment systems, billing models, or PSP integrations.
Observability and alerting — Prometheus, Grafana or equivalent.
Experience in the maritime, logistics or freight industry.
Familiarity with emissions accounting frameworks (GHG Protocol, GLEC, EU
ETS..).
Benefits
As part of our team, you will:

🌱 Have a chance to re-shape the future of climate in the logistics.
👩‍💻 Be empowered to deliver your best work remotely, and get a stipend to set
you up.
🏄‍♂️ Have a flat hierarchy, where you will have direct access to the founders
and won't be tied up in politics.
🎓 Have a high degree of learning and ownership in a dynamic environment.
🏝 Take part in our team-building events.

An overview of this role

As a Fullstack Engineer on the Duo Client SDK team at GitLab, you'll build the shared foundation for every GitLab Duo client. Today, the logic that powers Duo in editors lives inside the GitLab Language Server. We're extracting it into a true software development kit (SDK): a set of well-versioned TypeScript packages that editor extensions, our web-based Duo Chat on GitLab.com, and eventually external applications can use.

You'll work in TypeScript across frontend and backend systems. You'll design the SDK's Node.js core and public application programming interface (API), and work in the clients that use it. You'll have senior and staff engineers alongside you to help with design. You'll own the implementation of scoped packages and ship improvements with minimal guidance while collaborating with the team on larger architectural changes.

Some examples of our projects:

  • The Duo Client SDK, extracting versioned, publishable packages from the GitLab Language Server
  • The GitLab Language Server, rebuilt on top of the SDK as our polyglot surface
  • Duo Chat on the web, as one of the SDK's first consumers

What you'll do

  • Develop secure, well-tested, and performant TypeScript features that solve technical problems of moderate scope and complexity.
  • Ship small features and improvements with minimal guidance, writing tests with every merge request and contributing to code reviews and design discussions.
  • Extract and publish TypeScript packages from the GitLab Language Server, migrating consumers incrementally so no parallel implementation is left to drift.
  • Design durable public APIs with clear interfaces, semantic versioning, changelogs, and deprecation paths for external consumers.
  • Build isomorphic core packages that isolate platform-specific behavior in adapters at the edges.
  • Build and improve SDK client surfaces, including Vue 3 components in Duo Chat on the web, in collaboration with product, design, and engineering teams.
  • Strengthen credential handling across hosts, including bearer tokens, session cookies, and CSRF protection.
  • Optimize bundle size, startup cost, and dependency weight for browser consumers, and support a Tier 2 on-call rotation for urgent engineering issues.

What you'll bring

  • Strong proficiency with TypeScript across frontend and backend systems, including experience building and maintaining Node.js services.
  • Experience with modern build and packaging tools, including monorepos, multi-module builds, ECMAScript modules (ESM), and dependency management.
  • Experience with Vue 3 and the Composition API, or comparable component-based frontend experience and a willingness to learn Vue.
  • Experience designing APIs that other people use, with the ability to explain what you'd do differently.
  • Understanding of the differences between running code in Node.js and in the browser, and how to write code that works in both.
  • A security-minded development approach, including careful credential handling and performance optimization.
  • Ability to communicate clearly and concisely in writing about technical problems, propose iterative solutions, and work effectively in an agile environment.
  • Self-motivation, strong organizational skills, and the judgment to ask for help when needed while thriving in a fully remote organization aligned with GitLab's values.

The Duo Client SDK team sits in GitLab's AI Clients stage and works closely with teams building GitLab Duo experiences. We collaborate across client surfaces to make thoughtful technical decisions as the platform evolves. We work fully remotely and asynchronously across regions, in the open, following GitLab's values of transparency and open communication.

Proven professional experience in full stack software development and blockchain engineering.

description:
We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.

 

You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.

 

Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.

 

How it works

 

Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.

Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.

Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks.

Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.

Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.

Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.

Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another.

 

Requirements

 

2+ years of professional software engineering

Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code)

Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++

Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing

Regular use of an AI coding tool

Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models

You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words

At least 10 hours a week, starting now

A secure personal or work computer (no public or shared machines)

 

Nice to have

 

Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure

Experience building agent tasks or RL environments

 

Terms

 

US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you

Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms

The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us

Don't publish the work anywhere: no public pull request or public fork

 

Apply at https://www.askable.com/experts/roles/senior-software-engineer
